title: Understanding Compression Tap Leaks: Worn Valve Washers
description: When a compression tap drips, the instinct is often to crank the handle tighter. However, over-tightening is actually a primary cause of tap leaks. Inside the valve assembly, a rubber washer presses against a smooth brass valve seat to stop water flow. Forcing the handle down squashes and splits this rubber seal over time, creating small pathways for pressurized water to escape through the spout. If your tap continues to drip after light pressure is applied, cranking it harder will only ruin the washer completely. The proper fix is isolating the water supply, dismantling the valve stem, and replacing the degraded washer.

on_image_text.hook: Why Cranking a Dripping Tap Makes It Worse
on_image_text.explanation: Over-tightening squashes and splits the internal rubber washer against the valve seat.
on_image_text.takeaway: Replace the internal washer instead of forcing the handle closed.
